info.title: viz ruler API
info.description: Two faces over a tenant's rules and alerts. `/api/v1/rules` and `/api/v1/alerts` return Prometheus' own response shapes, read-only. `/api/v1/monitors/...` is viz's API. The tenant is always the one the API key belongs to; no path, query, header or body field selects it. Every write accepts `dryRun` (query parameter, or a `dryRun: true` body field): it validates and reports what would happen and changes nothing.

A saved monitor over a past range, as it is stored, at its interval: when it would have fired and resolved, with the explanation each alert would have carried

step.description: Default the monitor's interval (the only step for anomaly and SLO monitors)

apiKey.description: A viz API key (`viz_<keyId>_<secret>`), as Bearer or as the password of Basic. Scopes: monitors:read, monitors:write, monitors:ack. The key decides the tenant.

dryRun.name: dryRun
dryRun.description: Validate and report what would happen; change nothing.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, unknown, disabled or wrong API key

Forbidden.description: The key lacks the scope this operation needs

NotFound.description: No such resource for this tenant

BacktestRefused.description: Validation problems (`problems`), or `over_budget`: the read was refused before anything was fetched

path.description: The field, e.g. `condition.threshold` or `groups[0].rules[2].for`; `line 12` for a YAML error

threshold.description: In the unit the query returns: a ratio of 1% is 0.01

MonitorInput.description: Give either `expr`, or `query` with `condition`, or `query` with `anomaly`, or `slo` (no query).

group.description: Default: monitors/<interval> (anomaly monitors: anomalies/<interval>, SLO monitors: slos/<interval>), shared by monitors with the same interval

notify.description: A receiver name from the notifier config

noData.description: When the query returns nothing: resolve (ok), fire after noDataFor (alerting), or keep the last state (keep)

expr.description: Null for an SLO monitor (its SLI is the expression)

state.description: warming: an anomaly monitor whose detector has not scored anything yet, an SLO monitor whose windows hold too few buckets, or either while it is warmed from history

TimelineEntry.description: `source: ruler` entries are state transitions; `source: notifier` entries are notifications and what people did.

dropped.description: Entries dropped because the log is bounded; 0 means the history is complete

fingerprint.description: One alert; default: every firing alert of the monitor

Rule.description: A Prometheus rule: `alert` or `record`. viz adds no_data, no_data_for, no_data_expr and monitor to alerting rules, `anomaly` (an anomaly rule: `expr` is the series to watch and a detector decides which series alert) and `slo` (an SLO burn-rate rule, without `expr`). `expr` is required except for an SLO rule.

anomaly.description: detector, params, unit, severity, max_series (and given, written by the export). An export with extensions=false leaves anomaly rules out.

slo.description: objective, window, sli ({ bad, total }, { good, total } or { error_ratio }, each with $window), alerts ([{ severity, long_window, short_window, burn_rate }]), min_events, min_coverage, max_series (and given, written by the export). An export with extensions=false leaves SLO rules out.

BacktestRequest.description: Give `monitor` (the document you are about to save) or `rule` (a rule-file entry: alerting, anomaly or SLO). An anomaly or SLO rule runs at its interval (`step`, which `interval` must equal if given), its detector or windows warmed from the history before `fromMs`. Every read is planned first and refused whole over the budget (422 over_budget).

open.description: Still in this state at the end of the range

annotations.description: What the alert carried when it entered this state, templates expanded: for an anomaly or SLO alert, the explanation it would have been sent with

note.description: What this step can and cannot show

warmup.description: Anomaly and SLO rules: the history before fromMs fed through the rule (no alerts), as a warm-up would

cost.description: What the engine's plan said before the fetch, and the budget

memory.description: History is fetched and evaluated in windows of `windowSteps` steps (per read), one at a time, carrying only the rule's state: the modelled peak and the budget

cpu.description: The CPU model's cost of the run (modelled, not measured) and maxBacktestCpuMs

AnomalyInput.description: An anomaly monitor: `query` is the series to watch (a gauge, or rate() of a counter) and a detector, not a condition, decides when it alerts. Defaults follow held-out evidence (GET /api/v1/monitors/detectors): detector ewma with halfLifePoints 100 and k 8, or threshold when severity is page; severity ticket (info for cusum); for 0s and keepFiringFor 10m; maxSeries 100.

detector.description: Default ewma; threshold when severity is page (then params.above or params.below is required). stl, pelt and burn_rate are refused: they explain, they do not page.

params.description: The detector's parameters by name (anomaly/src/detectors). Not stepMs (the interval) or unit (use unit). Unknown names and wrong types are refused.

unit.description: Printed after numbers in the explanation, e.g. ms

maxSeries.description: Most series the query may return. Above it the evaluation is refused (state error, status series_cap_exceeded): nothing is scored and no alert changes; series are never dropped. Default 100.

AnomalyHistory.description: What the detector reads, classified like a rule's query (design §7).

minPoints.description: Valid points before anything is scored; until then the monitor is warming

status.description: A refused evaluation (series_cap_exceeded, state_limit_exceeded, state_unreadable) changes no state and no alert

series.description: Series the query returned at the last evaluation

missing.description: NaN or infinite points: not scored, the previous flag kept

inRules.description: Usable in a monitor; false: a library function for scheduled jobs and explanations

defaults.description: Parameters the ruler fills in beyond the library's own

defaultsValidated.description: True only when the defaults are the configuration scored on held-out data

params.description: Every parameter, defaults written out when saved

Warmup.description: How warming an anomaly or SLO rule from history went (contracts/rules.ts `WarmupStatus`, contract version 4). The read is planned first (the engine's plan, nothing fetched); over the budget it is refused whole and the rule starts cold.

status.description: pending: not run yet, or retried at the next tick after an engine failure; refused: over the budget or refused by the engine's plan, nothing fetched, the rule started cold; failed: the engine failed 3 times, the rule started cold

plan.description: What the engine's plan said before anything was fetched, summed over the range queries

points.description: Points fed through the rule's evaluation

SloInput.description: An SLO monitor (contract version 4): no query or condition; the SLI is the expression and the multi-window, multi-burn-rate alerts of the SRE Workbook decide (by default page 1h/5m at 14.4x and 6h/30m at 6x, ticket 1d/2h at 3x and 3d/6h at 1x). Each alert carries severity page or ticket. Default group slos/<interval>.

objective.description: Target fraction of good events, e.g. 0.999

sli.description: { bad, total }, { good, total } or { errorRatio }: PromQL with $window, which the ruler replaces with the bucket width (the interval), e.g. sum(increase(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[$window]))

minEvents.description: Events a long window must hold before its alert may fire (low-traffic guard). Default 0

minCoverage.description: Fraction of a window's buckets that must have data for the window to count. Default 0.9

maxSeries.description: Most series the SLI may return; above it the evaluation is refused. Default 10, at most 100

SloHistory.description: What an SLO rule reads: one bucket per tick; warming reads the longest alert window in buckets of the interval and the compliance window in coarser buckets.

status.description: A refused evaluation (series_cap_exceeded, invalid_result, state_unreadable) changes no state and no alert

burning.description: Series whose page / ticket condition held at the last evaluation

budgetRemaining.description: Lowest fraction of the error budget left over the series (negative once overspent)

budgetCoveredMs.description: How much of the compliance window that figure covers

OverBudget.description: Refused, whole, nothing kept: the modelled peak memory is over the backtest's memory budget (windows cannot be small enough to hold the rule's state and one step), the engine's plan of the read is over the backtest budget, the engine's own limits would refuse it, or its cost could not be asked (plan null); or the CPU model's projection of the whole run is over maxBacktestCpuMs (cpu set), found after reading the first window, whose series it counts, or a later one with more series

peakBytes.description: The memory model's peak: the rule's state, its alerts and intervals, and the largest window

memory.description: The memory model; null when the engine's plan refused before sizing

modelledMs.description: The CPU model's projection of the whole run (modelled, not measured)

cpu.description: The CPU model; null when another budget refused the run
